scout.purpose: The Level 4 capstone integrates coroutine ownership, Flow, resilient HTTP, pagination, persistence, queued writes, and durable synchronization into one observable data system.
scout.realWorldUse: A production news experience must launch without internet, refresh and page safely, preserve bookmarks, recover from failures, and explain its source-of-truth behaviour.
scout.outcome: Deliver a tested local-first vertical slice and defend its authority, freshness, idempotency, migration, and background-work decisions.

sections.title: Architecture starts from local reads and durable intent

blocks.text: The UI observes Room-backed article and bookmark state only. Retrofit and OkHttp fetch cursor pages into a remote data source; a repository maps DTOs and transactionally updates Room plus ETag, cursor, and freshness metadata. Paging uses Room PagingSource and RemoteMediator so network loads never bypass local authority. DataStore owns small sync and presentation preferences. ViewModels combine repository Flows into complete immutable UiState and retain paging generations.

blocks.caption: Local reads and transactional intent stay authoritative while network and persistent scheduling synchronize them.

blocks.text: Bookmark actions update local desired state and outbox rows atomically, then enqueue one unique WorkManager sync. The engine sends stable operation IDs, pauses for authentication, retries transient failures, reconciles rejection, and resolves documented version conflicts. Access-token refresh is single-flight and redacted. Article reads work without a session where product rules allow. Connectivity hints can prompt synchronization but actual requests determine outcomes. Stale content remains visible during failed refresh.

blocks.caption: Local reads and transactional intent stay authoritative while network and persistent scheduling synchronize them.

blocks.title: Offline-first is an authority model
blocks.text: It is more than catching IOException or adding a cache collection.

sections.title: Release evidence covers failure over time

blocks.text: Release evidence includes Room DAO and migration tests, DataStore update tests, Flow and virtual-time tests, PagingSource and RemoteMediator cases, MockWebServer protocol and retry tests, concurrent refresh tests, WorkManager scheduling tests, and a process-death manual script. Demonstrate first launch online, later launch offline, pagination, pull refresh, token expiry, bookmark while offline, process termination, connectivity restoration, conflict or rejection, and eventual convergence without duplicate server effects.

Production data work must remain correct after interruption and repetition. Define the source of truth, stable operation identity, transaction boundary, cancellation behaviour, and the state shown before remote confirmation. Exercise empty and stale data, malformed input, duplicate delivery, simultaneous callers, process death, schema upgrade, storage pressure, and connectivity restoration where relevant. Use pure unit tests for mapping and conflict policy, real Room or DataStore instances for persistence contracts, MockWebServer for protocol behaviour, and WorkManager test APIs for durable scheduling. Logs must reveal operation state without exposing tokens, user content, or personal identifiers. A future engineer should be able to explain which component owns every row, cursor, credential, retry, and final user-visible outcome.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name authority, identity, lifetime, failure, cancellation, and recovery.

steps.label: Persist intent
steps.detail: Commit user-visible state or queued work before unreliable boundaries.

steps.label: Execute
steps.detail: Perform the smallest idempotent or transactional operation.

steps.label: Reconcile
steps.detail: Merge authoritative outcome and resolve conflicts deliberately.

steps.label: Verify
steps.detail: Test interruption, recreation, migration, duplication, and offline recovery.

blocks.title: Do not certify only the online happy path
blocks.text: The project goal is recovery across time, duplication, process loss, and conflicting state.

inspect.title: Find the network-first launch
walkthrough: Opening the feed blocks on network before reading durable local content.
The returned remote list bypasses the declared Room source of truth.
Observe Room immediately and run refresh as a separate operation that writes into it.
inspect.expectedOutput: A previously synchronized feed opens offline and updates through the same Room-backed stream after refresh.

trap_check.mistake: Marking a bookmark confirmed when only local optimistic state committed.
trap_check.why: The UI cannot explain pending, rejection, or conflict after restart.
trap_check.fix: Persist and expose pending synchronization state until remote reconciliation.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a retry, cache, or abstraction without naming the failure contract.
trap_check.why: The implementation hides ambiguity while duplicate, stale, or lost outcomes remain possible.
trap_check.fix: Write the invariant and an interruption test before introducing machinery.

challenge_intro.task: Build the full Level 4 news slice with Room source of truth, cursor paging, ETag refresh, DataStore settings, secure session refresh, bookmark outbox, WorkManager sync, conflicts, migrations, and layered tests.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Previously synchronized articles and bookmarks work offline. Process death and duplicate delivery lose no accepted intent. Paging, authentication, migrations, retries, and eventual convergence have deterministic evidence.

recall.prompt: What should the feed UI observe?

recall.answer: Tests showing local and server state agree after retry and conflict policy.
